test_title: RRB NTPC CBT 2 (Level-2) Official Paper (Held On: 16 June 2022 Shift 2)
subject: general
question: Two poles are on either side of a road. A 20 m long ladder is placed between the two poles. When the ladder rests against one pole, it makes an angle of 60° with the pole and when it is turned to rest against the other pole, it makes an angle of 30° with the road. Calculate the width of the road. (in m) (Use sqrt 3 = 1.732)
solution:
**GIVEN:**

Two poles 

20 m long ladder which makes an angle of 60 with one pole and an angle of 30 with other on turning.

**FORMULA USED:**

 sin60^circ =(sqrt3)/(2) 

 cos30^circ = (sqrt3)/(2)

** CALCULATION:**

** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/889350708ee47f95bdc28d9e58f5fbc7b99ba3d86e7184b703df6dbac9006bab.png] **

Let the pole be AB and CD respectively

BD be the width where BD=BE+ED

Let the ladder be AE with one pole and CE be the ladder on turning with other pole

Hence Pole AB makes an angle of 60 with ladder AE

sin 60= perpendicular/hypotenuse=BE/AE

 (sqrt3)/(2) = BE/20

BE = 10 × sqrt3 = (10 × 1.73) = 17.3

On turning with other pole ladder becomes EC makes an angle of 30 with the road

COS 30° = Base/hypotenuse

ED/EC=ED/20

 (sqrt3)/(2) =ED/20

ED=10 × sqrt3

(10 × 1.73) = 17.3

Width of the road =(17.3+17.3) = 34.6

**∴ Width of the road is 34.6 m. **
